description:
pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:186-205 (find_parent) decodes both AKI on `cert` and SKI on every `candidate` in `bundle` on every call. reaches_self_signed (lines 139-175) calls find_parent up to bundle.len()+1 times. Net: O(N²) DER decode calls for a bundle of size N during a single signer-discovery construction.

Today's bundles in PKITS §4.5 are 2-3 certs, so this is microseconds. The concern is pkix-chain composing this with pkix-path-builder, which can hand pkix-revocation a bundle assembled from a much larger trust store + intermediate cache (50-500 certs in real deployments).

x509-cert's Extension::from_der is not free — it allocates and runs ASN.1 state. For a 500-cert bundle, that's 250000 decode calls in the worst case, with allocations.

Fix: build a SKI lookup table at the top of reaches_self_signed: HashMap<&[u8], &Certificate> keyed by SKI bytes (or a slice-of-pairs if no_std-friendly). Bundle traversal becomes O(N) decode + O(1) lookup per step, total O(N) for the walk. Pkix-revocation already has std (the crl feature requires std per Cargo.toml line 22), so std HashMap is available.

Not a hot path today; flagged for when bundles grow.
title: Per-cert SKI/AKI re-decoded on every iteration of reaches_self_signed
